title: Compatible lifting of an idempotent to the formal-fibre section limit
statement: Let f:X→S be a morphism of schemes, s∈S, A=O_(S,s) and m its maximal ideal. Use the formal-fibre section system [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology]: X_n=Spec(A/m^(n+1))×_S X, its section modules over the completed ring, and restriction transitions. For every idempotent e∈Γ(X_0,O), there exists an element v of the inverse limit of these section modules whose zeroth projection equals e. No properness, Noetherian or henselian hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: For A = O_(S,s), set m = maximalIdeal A. The map X_0 to X_n is the base change of A/m^(n+1) to A/m. The image ideal m/m^(n+1) has (n+1)st power zero. Pasting pullbacks and identifying the double quotient identifies the base change with X_0, compatibly with its projections.

Apply nilpotent_baseChange_idempotents to the first projection X_n to Spec(A/m^(n+1)) and the image ideal m/m^(n+1). Transport its unique idempotent lift along the preceding identification to obtain e_n on X_n restricting to e on X_0. This is uniqueness among idempotents; no surjectivity on all sections is asserted.

The transition X_n to X_(n+1) followed by restriction from X_0 is restriction from X_0. Pullback preserves idempotents. Consequently e_(n+1) restricts to e_n by uniqueness. The compatible family determines an element v of the concrete inverse limit of modules over the completed ring, and its zeroth component is e. This includes e = 0, e = 1 and empty fibres; it does not require the two clopen pieces to be nonempty.
